# Body-merge vectors

Cross-implementation vectors for the three-way text merge: the browser kit's
TypeScript (`web/apps/src/kit/coedit/pendingIntent.ts`) and its Rust port
(`src/coedit/body_merge.rs`). Design: `docs/design/body-merge-home.md` section 1.

Both suites run **every** case in **every** `*.json` file here:

- Rust: `cargo test --lib coedit::body_merge`
- TS: `cd web/apps && npx vitest run test/coedit/bodyMerge.vectors.test.ts`

**TypeScript is the producer of record.** The files are generated by running the
kit's TS over the case definitions, then reviewed by hand against the design.
Do not edit them; change `web/apps/test/coedit/generateBodyMergeVectors.ts` and run

```
cd web/apps && npx vite-node test/coedit/writeBodyMergeVectors.ts
```

The vitest runner regenerates in memory and fails if the checked-in files differ,
so a change to the TS merge shows up as a vector diff.

## Format

```json
{ "format": "body-merge-vectors/1", "unit": "unicode_scalars", "description": "...",
  "cases": [ { "name": "...", "category": "...", "note": "...",
               "base": S, "mine": S, "theirs": S,
               "hunks": [ {"index": 4, "del": 5, "insert": "frosty"} ],
               "expect": { ... } } ] }
```

- **Unit: Unicode scalars.** Every offset and length is a scalar index (not
  bytes, not UTF-16). The TS runner converts at the boundary. Lone surrogates
  cannot be represented, so those cases stay TS-only
  (`pendingIntent.rebase.test.ts`).
- `S` is a string, or a recipe both runners expand: `{"repeat": S, "times": n}`
  or `{"concat": [S, ...]}`. Cap-sized inputs are written this way.
- `hunks` present: run `rebase_hunks` with exactly those hunks (the TS test
  surface); `mine` is `base` with them applied. Absent: derive hunks by diffing
  `base`→`mine` (`hunks_between`), i.e. the `merge_bodies` pipeline.
- `expect` (compared whole by both runners):
  `regions` = `diff_regions(base, theirs)`; `hunks` (derived cases only);
  `placed` (theirs coordinates); `clashes` (`base_start`, `base_end`, `base`,
  `mine`, `theirs`, `theirs_start`, `theirs_end`); `draft`;
  `unreplayed_deletes`; `merged` = theirs with the placed hunks applied; `at` =
  per clash `{at_start, at_end}` in the merged text.
- Any string longer than 256 scalars is recorded as `{"len": n, "sha256": hex}`
  (scalar length, SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes) to keep cap cases small.
- Every clash must satisfy `merged[at_start..at_end] == theirs`; both runners
  assert it for all cases, as well as `base[base_start..base_end] == base` and
  `theirs[theirs_start..theirs_end] == theirs`.

## Categories

`kit-placement`, `kit-adjacency`, `kit-unicode`, `parity` (identical change
clashes), `property-*` (the two fixed-seed loops of the kit test, exported
once), `cap-line`, `cap-char`, `cap-char-scope` (a capped block separated from
another edit by an equal line), `s8.3a-deletion`, `ambiguity-pair`,
`must-not-extend`, `lineage` (3.5 worked examples as single `merge_bodies`
calls), `merge-bodies`.
